question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $W$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[3,10],$ compute $P(W\le 5).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $W$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(w)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le w\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $W$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[3,10],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(w)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{7},\, & 3\le w\le 10, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W\le 5) & =P(3\le W\le 5) \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}f(w)\,\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{5}\frac{1}{7}\,\text{d}w \\  & =\frac{5-3}{7} \\  & =\frac{2}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
